question.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
3{x}_{1}^{2}\le 6{x}_{1}^{2},\,4{x}_{3}^{2}\le 6{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \le 6{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=6(1)=6.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\le 6.$ 

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $6.$ But before we conclude that $6$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=6.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3(0)^{2}+6(1)^{2}+4(0)^{2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the maximum value of  $Q(x)$ is equal to $6.$
